messages:
maria: Quick post — ran a focused perf pass on INT8/FP8 paths comparing prefill vs decode on long-context Llama2-70B. Surprising regression on decode when KV cache is quantized.
kevin: Can you paste the profiler snippets? which kernels were selected for prefill vs decode?
maria: Prefill was hitting packed4-int8 GEMM (fast), decode fell back to dequantize+fp16-gemm for each attention because our KV lookup returns quantized tensors and current kernels expect fp16 key/vals. Profiler:
```
# prefill (batch 8, seq 1024)
compute_attention_kernel: 42ms
packed4_int8_gemm: 110ms (total)
overall_prefill_latency: 370ms
# decode (auto-batched, 1 token each, long ctx cached)
kv_dequantize+copy: 18ms per step
fp16_attn_gemm: 24ms per step
overall_decode_ttft: 120ms (first token slower than expected)
```
julia: So prefill TPS looked good but TTFT for decode increased because of dequantize overhead per step? That matches the numbers.
sam: Do we do dequantize on CPU or GPU? Moving that to fused GPU kernel could help a lot.
maria: Currently dequantize happens on GPU but as a separate kernel pass. Two copies: quantized KV -> dequantize kernel -> fp16 buffer -> attn kernel. That extra launch hurts single-token TTFT even though amortized TPS is good for big prefill batches.
kevin: Could we keep KV in quantized representation and implement attention kernels that consume qkv directly (scaled int8/4-bit inputs)? That avoids dequantize step.
julia: We already have int8 prefill kernels, but decode uses fp16 kernels for stability. There's a quality/regression risk if we switch decode to int8 kernels without recalibration.
maria: Right. We tried switching decode to packed4-int8 and saw a ~20% TTFT improvement, but generation quality dropped on a few long-context prompt cases (token repetition and soft-max skew).
perf-bot: perf/regression-alert: model=llama2-70b, change=decode-int8-fastpath, perf_delta_ttft=-18%, quality_alert=+1.9 BLEU-regression-equivalent
sam: What about a hybrid heuristic: use fp16-decode for initial N tokens after context (sensitive window), then switch to int8 decode afterwards? Or use a confidence metric to toggle.
kevin: Hybrid helps quality but switching cost may reintroduce memcpy/format conversion overhead. Need to quantify the cost of a single-mode switch vs per-token dequant.
maria: Proposed routing heuristics (config example):
```
"kernel_routing": {
  "decode_threshold_tokens": 64,
  "prefer_int8_for_decode_after": true,
  "kv_keep_quantized": true,
  "calibration_profile": "per-model-longctx-v2"
}
```
This means: while generated_tokens < 64 use fp16 decode path, after that use int8 fused-attn that consumes quantized KV.
julia: Also suggest per-model calibration pass that collects scale/zero for attention heads on long prefixes. Calibration reduces quality gap for int8 decode.
kevin: Any numbers for hybrid? maria: On a 2048-context test with batched prefill, hybrid gives: prefill TPS +8% (same), decode TTFT improvement ~12% vs pure fp16 decode, quality drop reduced to ~0.6% vs 1.9% when using full int8 decode.
sam: For routing, we should add a fast path detection: if incoming request has num_prompts>1 and avg_len small -> prefer decode-optimized fused kernels (TTFT critical). If single long-context streaming -> prefer prefill-optimized TPS kernels.
maria: Also flagged a perf regression: a recent kernel selector change (auto-fallback to stable fp16 for decode) didn't respect kv_keep_quantized flag; it forces a dequant path. Patch in review: https://git.redwood/changes/1234 fixes selection priority.
kevin: Quick checklist: (1) implement fused int8-attn decode kernel prototype (2) add per-model calibration harness for long-ctx (3) add routing flags + CI perf checks for TTFT vs TPS tradeoffs (4) test hybrid switching cost.
julia: Can we add an eval set focusing on repetition/coverage for long contexts to catch quality regressions automatically? I can seed with 120 prompts.
maria: Yes please. Also I pushed a small perf benchmark script to repo:
```
./bench/quant_prefill_decode.sh --model llama2-70b --ctx 2048 --trials 50
```

sam: Thanks — let's aim to land the kernel selector fix + calibration harness in next sprint. If anyone wants the raw traces I uploaded them to gcp://redwood-perf/1799123456/traces.tar.gz
